exposure: Age at first pregnancy (<19 years vs. ≥19 years)
cohort: 400 women in one community of Northern Ghana
finding: Adolescent women (<19 years at their first pregnancy) have a higher risk for cesarean section, stillbirth, and neonatal death in subsequent pregnancies compared to older women (≥19 years).
mod_finding: Adolescent women (<19 years at their first pregnancy) have an 80% higher risk for a cesarean section for the first and subsequent births as compared to older women (≥ 19 years).
